name: Online grocery delivery
title: Why Webvan failed, and when online grocery became viable
question: Why did Webvan fail, and when did online grocery become viable?
answer: Webvan built its own automated warehouses and truck fleet, lost over $800M, and filed for bankruptcy in July 2001. The business that later worked, Instacart (2012), owned neither: it sent gig shoppers to existing stores, dispatched by smartphone. The missing piece was a cheap way to dispatch labour, not demand.
verdict_reason: Smartphone ownership passed 45% of US adults in 2012, the year Instacart was founded.

constraint.name: Smartphone dispatch and gig labour
constraint.detail: Without phones in shoppers' and drivers' pockets, delivery needed owned warehouses and salaried drivers: fixed costs that grocery margins could not cover.
